title: Review B6 (T-0029): base_for, scoped_diff base, review affinity and executing-account skip
spec: Adversarial review of commit(s) on task/T-0029 (your worktree is based on that branch; verify `grep base_for orchestrator/spawn.py` first). Focus: (1) base_for never returns a branch that does not exist; falls back to origin/main; behaves when inputs is empty or inputs[0] is a dict (challenge tasks carry a dict, not a task id); (2) ensure_worktree still honours an explicit base argument; (3) scoped_diff uses `<goal>...HEAD` only when the goal branch exists and never raises when the reviewed task has no parent; (4) Pool.pick("review") skips the executing account only when another account has headroom, and still returns an account when only the executing one is free (never None just because of the skip); (5) pool.toml still parses and account A's affinity gained review without losing planner reserve semantics; (6) tests build real branches in a scratch repo rather than mocking git. Run `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py` and report the result line. Return ONLY {"verdict":"approve|request_changes","comments":[...]} under 3,000 chars.

comments.issue: base_for's role in ("review","challenge") check is dead for challenge tasks: spawn_challenge always sets inputs[0] to a {claim,evidence,confidence} dict (see mcp.py spawn_challenge docstring), never a task-id string, so isinstance(...,str) is always False for role='challenge'. Every challenge worktree silently falls back to origin/main, contradicting README.md's new claim that 'review and challenge worktrees are based on the reviewed task's own branch.' No test covers base_for with role='challenge'.

Disabled placeholder rows luna6/terra6/sol6 omit quota_group (unlike astra/luna/terra/sol which all set quota_group="chatgpt"). Harmless while disabled, but the row comments say to flip enabled=true once the id appears in models_cache.json - if that happens without also adding quota_group, a usage-limit hit won't cool the whole chatgpt group correctly across gpt-5.6/gpt-6 variants.
Test result: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_orchestrator -v` -> Ran 39 tests in 7.452s, OK (0 failures, 0 errors).
